extra_misconceptions.fact: The diesel engine drives an alternator that generates electricity to power electric traction motors geared directly to each wheel axle.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern diesel-electric locomotives use a mechanical transmission and driveshaft to connect the diesel engine directly to the drive wheels.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Manifest trains stop repeatedly at classification yards for switching, while unit trains move nonstop from one origin to one destination.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mixed manifest freight trains travel faster coast-to-coast than unit trains because they carry lighter, higher-priority retail boxes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The Surface Transportation Board classifies railroads into Class I, II, or III based strictly on annual operating revenue thresholds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Railroad classification tracks are determined primarily by the total route mileage a carrier operates across North America.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Federal Hours of Service laws limit duty to twelve hours, requiring fresh operating crews to swap at designated crew change points.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Locomotive engineers stay aboard the same freight train for its entire cross-country trip by sleeping in a rear caboose.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to transit time when a unit coal train bypasses intermediate classification hump yards on its route?
Which component converts mechanical energy from the diesel prime mover into electrical current for the axle traction motors?
What operational factors determine the spacing of crew change points along a Class I railroad mainline subdivision?
Why is double-stacking intermodal shipping containers in well cars more fuel-efficient than hauling highway trailers on flatcars?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Outside the Northeast Corridor, Amtrak operates mainly as a tenant over tracks owned, maintained, and dispatched by freight railroads.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Amtrak owns and dispatches almost all of the railroad track mileage that its long-distance passenger trains use nationwide.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Light rail uses electric streetcars on urban corridors, whereas commuter rail runs heavier trains on mainline tracks from outer suburbs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Light rail transit and commuter rail are identical systems that differ only in the paint scheme used by the local transit agency.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Railroad passenger timetables always print arrival and departure times in the local time zone of each individual station stop.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Timetable departure and arrival times for cross-country passenger trains are listed exclusively in Eastern Standard Time.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-speed trains use overhead catenary wires and pantographs because third-rail shoes cannot maintain safe contact at high speeds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: High-speed electric passenger trains draw power from a third rail mounted alongside the running rails at over 125 miles per hour.

extra_socratic_questions: What economic crisis in the late 1960s led Congress to pass the Rail Passenger Service Act creating Amtrak in 1971?
Which timetable details must you check when planning a 500-mile rail journey across two different time zones?
What engineering features distinguish grade-separated heavy rail subways from street-running light rail transit systems?
Under what operating conditions can intercity passenger trains share mainline tracks with slower freight trains safely?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The Engineering Department maintains track, bridges, and signals, while the Mechanical Department services locomotives and railcars.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Mechanical Department maintains track switches, wooden crossties, bridges, and wayside signal masts across the railroad.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Railroads purchase or lease locomotives and freight cars from specialized outside support manufacturers such as Wabtec and Greenbrier.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Railroad companies manufacture all of their own diesel-electric locomotives and freight cars inside their internal repair shops.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Freight conductors oversee train makeup, air brake tests, waybills, switching moves, and Federal Railroad Administration track authorities.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Freight train conductors spend their shift walking through cars to punch passenger tickets rather than managing train operations.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Maintenance-of-way workers must obtain formal track and time authority from the dispatcher before fouling any active mainline track.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Track maintenance crews can enter an active mainline track at any time without contacting the train dispatcher first.

extra_socratic_questions: Which railroad department is responsible for inspecting steel rail defects, replacing crossties, and surfacing track ballast?
What specific duties separate the conductor from the locomotive engineer inside the operating cab of a freight train?
Why do shippers and railroads often lease specialty tank cars from third-party railcar leasing companies instead of buying them?
What safety certifications must a railroader maintain to work in the mechanical, signal, or transportation departments?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Running at a 45-degree angle toward the approaching train keeps you clear of flying vehicle debris once the locomotive strikes the car.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: When a car stalls on a railroad crossing with a train approaching, you should run away in the same direction the train is traveling.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Trains cannot steer off the rails, and a loaded freight train at 55 miles per hour requires more than a mile to come to a complete stop.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A locomotive engineer who spots a pedestrian or stalled car on the tracks can steer away or brake to a stop within a few hundred feet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Locomotives and freight cars overhang the steel rails by at least three feet on both sides, creating a lethal strike zone near the ties.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standing just outside the steel rails is safe because locomotives and freight cars are no wider than the track gauge itself.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern welded rail and aerodynamic rolling stock make approaching trains surprisingly quiet until they are dangerously close.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hearing no train horn or rail vibration means that no train is approaching a bridge, tunnel, or curve along the right-of-way.

extra_socratic_questions: Why should you evacuate at a 45-degree angle toward the approaching train if your vehicle stalls on a grade crossing?
Which two pieces of information on the blue Emergency Notification System sign must you report first to the railroad dispatcher?
Why is it dangerous to stand within three feet of the outer rail even when you are not stepping directly on the crossties?
What physical factors require a loaded freight train traveling at 55 miles per hour to take more than a mile to stop?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A railroad crossbuck is a regulatory sign that requires every driver to yield the right-of-way to any approaching train.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A white railroad crossbuck is merely a decorative marker that indicates where tracks intersect a public road without legal duty.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Flashing red lights indicate a second train may be approaching on an adjacent track, and driving around lowered gates is illegal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Once the last car of a train clears a crossing, it is safe to drive around flashing red lights that have not yet turned off.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The round yellow RXR sign is an advance warning sign installed several hundred feet ahead of the crossing so drivers can slow down.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The round yellow RXR sign is placed directly at the edge of the railroad tracks to mark the exact stopping line for vehicles.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Passive crossings without active gates still carry live train traffic, requiring drivers to look, listen, and yield before proceeding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Grade crossings without automated gates or flashing lights are abandoned rail lines where trains no longer operate.

extra_socratic_questions: What functional difference separates a passive white crossbuck sign from an active flashing-light grade crossing signal?
Why must a driver remain stopped behind the white stop bar after one train clears a crossing equipped with a multi-track plaque?
Under what roadway conditions do traffic engineers mount flashing red crossing lights on an overhead cantilever mast?
Which advance warning sign alerts drivers of low-boy trailers or motorhomes that a raised grade crossing may snag their undercarriage?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Block signals use low-voltage electrical track circuits that are shorted out when steel wheels and axles bridge the two running rails.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wayside block signals rely solely on overhead cameras and radar sensors to detect whether a train occupies a section of track.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An End-of-Train Device radios rear brake pipe air pressure to the cab and can trigger an emergency brake application from the rear.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Flashing Rear-End Device is only a battery-powered red taillight mounted to make the last freight car visible at night.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Federal rules mandate the exact sequence of two long, one short, and one long horn blast approaching every public grade crossing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Locomotive engineers blow long and short horn blasts at crossings using personal style rather than standardized federal rules.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Swinging a hand, flag, or light horizontally at right angles across the track is the universal railroad signal to stop immediately.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Waving both arms vertically up and down above your head is the standard railroad hand signal for an emergency stop.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the low-voltage electrical track circuit when steel train wheels and axles enter an occupied signal block?
Why can a two-way End-of-Train Device still apply emergency air brakes from the rear if a blockage crimps the brake pipe mid-train?
Which locomotive horn pattern must an engineer sound at least 15 seconds before entering a public highway-rail grade crossing?
What hand or lantern motion across the track tells an approaching locomotive crew to make an immediate emergency stop?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A larger denominator in the scale ratio means greater reduction, so 1:160 N scale models are roughly half the size of 1:87 HO models.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A bigger numerical scale ratio such as 1:160 N scale produces physically larger model trains than 1:87 HO scale.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard DC controls track voltage for every engine in that block at once, whereas Digital Command Control addresses each decoder.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Conventional direct-current track power lets operators control the speed of three locomotives independently on a single uninsulated block.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Railroad rights-of-way are private property, and railfans must photograph trains only from public property or designated viewing platforms.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Railfans may step onto the ballast shoulder alongside mainline tracks to take photographs whenever no train is in sight.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Coarse sandpaper scratches microscopic grooves into the railhead that trap dirt and accelerate arcing, worsening electrical pickup.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cleaning model railroad track with coarse sandpaper improves electrical conductivity between the nickel-silver rails and locomotive wheels.

extra_socratic_questions: What trade-offs between minimum curve radius and benchwork space must you weigh when choosing between N scale and HO scale?
Why does a reverse loop on a two-rail model railroad layout create a direct electrical short circuit without insulated rail gaps?
Where must a railfan stand when photographing trains near a highway grade crossing to stay compliant with trespassing laws?
Which electrical wiring difference allows Digital Command Control to run multiple model locomotives independently on the same track?
